on/off, hundreds of times a second" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="34" width="150" x="286" y="120" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="w0" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=none;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#444;"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="276" y="188" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="300" y="188" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="w1" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=none;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#444;"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="420" y="188" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="470" y="188" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="buzz" parent="1" style="ellipse;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#d1c4e9;strokeColor=#6a1b9a;fontSize=11;fontStyle=1;" value="🔊
buzzer
(piezo disc)" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="76" width="90" x="470" y="150" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="w2" edge="1" parent="1" style="endArrow=none;html=1;strokeWidth=3;strokeColor=#444;"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <Array as="points"> <mxPoint x="620" y="188" /> <mxPoint x="620" y="298" /> </Array> <mxPoint x="560" y="188" as="sourcePoint" /> <mxPoint x="246" y="298" as="targetPoint" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="phys" parent="1" style="rounded=1;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;fillColor=#eef6ff;strokeColor=#4a90d9;fontSize=12;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;spacing=8;" value="⚡ <b>Physics:</b> inside is a <i>piezo</i> disc — a material that flexes when voltage is applied. Push-release it fast and it pumps the air, and air pressure waves are what your ears call sound. <b>PWM</b> (Pulse-Width Modulation) switches GPIO 4 on/off very quickly; the <b>frequency</b> of that switching = the <b>pitch</b> (440 times/sec = the note A). Double the frequency = one octave higher. The <b>duty</b> (how long it's on each cycle) sets the volume. That's the whole music trick from play_melody.py." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="760" x="60" y="370" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div: ⚡ Physics: inside is a piezo disc — a material that flexes when voltage is applied. Push-release it fast and it pumps the air, and air pressure waves are what your ears call sound. PWM (Pulse-Width Modulation) switches GPIO 4 on/off very quickly; the frequency of that switching = the pitch (440 times/sec = the note A). Double the frequency = one octave higher. The duty (how long it's on each cycle) sets the volume. That's the whole music trick from play_melody.py.
